The Blue Planet Where It Rains Glass Sideways

HD 189733b looks like a deep blue marble, but its winds blow at thousands of km/h and may carry silicate particles: glass, flying sideways.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

segments.text: There's a beautiful blue planet out there. But you'd never want to stand in its rain.
It's called HD 189733b, about sixty-four light-years from us.
segments.headline: 64 light-years away

segments.text: From far away it looks deep blue, like Earth. But it's a gas giant, roasting close to its star.
segments.headline: Blue, but deadly

segments.text: Winds there blow at about eight thousand seven hundred kilometers per hour.
Scientists think its clouds hold tiny bits of silicate, the stuff glass is made of.
segments.headline: Clouds of glass

segments.text: So the rain might be glass, flying sideways at seven times the speed of sound.
And in 2024, the Webb telescope found it smells like rotten eggs.
